sections.approach: The implementation follows a strict pipeline as specified in the bounty description, ensuring each rule is applied in order. First, transliteration is performed using a mapping table for specific characters (ß, ẞ, æ, Æ, ø, Ø, œ, Œ, đ, Đ, ł, Ł, þ, Þ, ð, Ð) to their ASCII equivalents before any normalization, as required. This ensures characters like 'ß' become 'ss' early. Next, Unicode NFKD normalization decomposes compatibility forms (e.g., ligatures, roman numerals, circled digits) into base characters and combining marks. Combining marks in the range U+0300-U+036F are then removed, leaving only the base characters. Apostrophes (both straight ' and curly ’) are removed without inserting separators, so contractions like "Don't" become "dont". The string is lowercased to meet the [a-z0-9] character set requirement. Word boundaries are identified by splitting on any character outside [a-z0-9], including spaces, punctuation, and non-ASCII characters (e.g., CJK scripts), which are effectively dropped. Words are defined as non-empty runs of [a-z0-9]. These words are joined with the specified separator (default '-'), ensuring no leading, trailing, or repeated separators. If maxLength is provided, the slug is truncated to fit: if the slug exceeds maxLength, the longest prefix of whole words that fits is used; if even the first word is longer than maxLength, that word is cut to maxLength characters, and no trailing separator is emitted. Empty or whitespace/punctuation-only inputs return an empty string. Idempotency is guaranteed by ensuring the pipeline produces a stable output that, when re-slugified with the same options, yields the same result. Input validation throws TypeError for non-string inputs and RangeError for invalid separator or maxLength values.
sections.edge_cases: Key edge cases handled include: 1) Empty strings or inputs containing only whitespace/punctuation return an empty string. 2) Repeated separators (e.g., 'a--b') are collapsed into a single separator. 3) Leading and trailing separators are removed entirely. 4) Transliteration of specific characters like sharp s (ß/ẞ -> ss), ligatures (æ/Æ -> ae, ø/Ø -> o, œ/Œ -> oe), and others (đ/Đ -> d, ł/Ł -> l, þ/Þ -> th, ð/Ð -> d) is applied correctly. 5) Unicode compatibility characters (e.g., ligatures like 'ﬁ' -> 'fi', roman numerals like 'Ⅻ' -> 'XII', circled digits like '①' -> '1') are decomposed via NFKD and normalized. 6) Non-Latin scripts (e.g., CJK characters) are treated as word boundaries and dropped, leaving only ASCII [a-z0-9] runs. 7) Apostrophes (both straight and curly) are removed without adding separators, so "Rock’n’Roll" becomes "rocknroll". 8) When maxLength is set and the first word exceeds it, the word is truncated to maxLength characters (e.g., "Supercalifragilistic" with maxLength=5 becomes "super"). 9) Idempotency is maintained: slugifying the output again with the same options yields the same string. 10) Invalid inputs throw appropriate errors: TypeError for non-string input, RangeError for separator not in ['-', '_', '.'] or maxLength not a positive integer.
